analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 956-989, a new 'shape warmup' paragraph block in the model-calibration section). It is documentation only, so no executable code, trust boundary, key handling or authorization path changes in this PR. The text describes an excluded warmup run once per loaded EngineV2 engine. It uses local-only probes (a 128-token greedy probe run twice, plus shape cells) that train no rate or counter, with a 20 s wall budget. It runs after the startup self-test and before registration, or before a standalone listener opens. The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env var (0 or always) is a performance toggle that the launchd job forwards.

Security-relevant considerations checked against the threat model:
- Prompt data (A-001): the warmup uses synthetic probes under the existing local-only calibration path. The docs do not claim it touches consumer data.
- Prefix cache (T-041): the docs say probes are uncached solo runs. They do not describe any SSD cache donation, so the at-rest surface and the SEC-035 acceptance are unchanged. If the implementation donated warmup prompts to the encrypted SSD cache, that would need a check, but the docs do not say so and the source is not supplied.
- Availability: the warmup is bounded by a 20 s budget, preemptible by customer requests, and gated before registration. The doc claim that startup warmup runs before registration is unverified against code. Nothing in the diff shows a regression.
- No new endpoints, secrets, attestation or serving-authorization changes (TB-011, A-016) are present.

Remaining unverified: whether the implementing code (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup) matches the docs, since no code was supplied. No finding is warranted from the docs alone.
